cases.oracle: BIND dig 9.20 +tls with +tls-ca against the dns-tls peer (RFC 7858: RFC 1035 TCP framing inside TLS) using the guest-generated throwaway CA; other-ca.pem did not sign the leaf

cases.candidate_script:
export PATH=/empty
export BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF="$PWD/resolv.conf"; dns query www.example.test A --doh "https://127.0.0.1:$FIXTURE_PORT/dns-query"
cases.reference_script:
set -o pipefail
curl --http1.1 --silent --show-error --fail --cacert /etc/ssl/cert.pem -H "Content-Type: application/dns-message" --data-binary @doh-query.bin "https://127.0.0.1:$FIXTURE_PORT/dns-query" | /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys,struct,ipaddress
b=sys.stdin.buffer.read()
assert len(b)==50, (len(b),b)
id,flags,qd,an,ns,ar=struct.unpack("!6H",b[:12])
assert id==0x1234 and flags&0x8000 and flags&15==0 and (qd,an,ns,ar)==(1,1,0,0)
assert b[12:34]==bytes.fromhex("03777777076578616d706c6504746573740000010001"), b[12:34]
assert b[34:36]==b"\xc0\x0c"
typ,cls,ttl,n=struct.unpack("!HHIH",b[36:46]);assert (typ,cls,n)==(1,1,4)
print(ipaddress.IPv4Address(b[46:50]))
'
cases.oracle: RFC 8484 POST application/dns-message over HTTPS. Reference: upstream curl HTTP/1.1 sends a fixed RFC 1035 A query; independent struct/ipaddress decoding asserts the response ID, flags, section counts, question, A record type/class/length, and prints its address. Both sides use the guest-installed public fixture CA.
cases.comparison: Answer output and decoded HTTP method/path/content-type plus DNS question fields; HTTP version is HTTP/1.1. BIND dig uses HTTP/2 and is not an oracle against this HTTP/1.1-only peer.; candidate runs with an exported empty PATH and must reach the peer using the enabled builtins
